steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 60.24 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Rip it flush
steps.text: This piece stands taller than the frame. Rip 1.43 in off the bark side, parallel to the stick's length, so it sits flush with both faces of the panel. Lay it on a sawn face on the bandsaw or table saw; tilt the blade 22.50° (half the slice's angle) so the cut runs square to the slice's centre line.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the RIGHT of the blade. Mitre 0° (square across). Bevel 0° (blade upright). Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, left of the blade, is a square-ended block 0.50 in long. This cut meets the side of the next ring piece.

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 0° (square across). Bevel 0° (blade upright). Measure from the first cut and mark: 59.49 in along the point; 59.49 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 59.49 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the ripped face -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is a square-ended block 12.01 in long -- keep it: it is long enough for a shorter piece. This cut meets the side of the next ring piece.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 59.49 in along the point, 59.49 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face, 59.49 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as ring 1, long side: standing on its point, bark toward the open side.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).
Rip flush: the standing pieces are taller than the frame; rip 1.43 in off the bark so they sit flush with both faces.

Lay the rings from the frame inward. Each ring is a small frame: three pieces in the same pinwheel as the frame -- each runs from the far side of the piece behind it to the near side of the piece ahead, square-cut both ends in plan.
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
Centre: a triangle 3.9 in across its inscribed circle is left. Fill it with a plug cut from one wedge laid flat, or leave it open as a vent.
fitting: Standing pieces meet the 45° slope at an angle: the first one's sawn face leans 22.5° off the slope -- plane it to suit, or start with a flipped wedge to turn the slope upright.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.
